https://www.delfi.lt/en/business/electri.text: Delfi EN Delfi Business 2026.09.02 16:55 Electricity price up by 5% in August Translated by Karolis Broga Source: Elta EN Electricity price up by 5% in August PHOTO: Dainius Labutis | Elta Follow Delfi on Google In August 2026, compared with July 2026, the average wholesale price of electricity in Lithuania increased by 5%, reaching EUR 80 per megawatt hour (MWh). According to Lithuania’s electricity transmission system operator Litgrid, electricity prices rose in all Baltic States in August. The average wholesale price in Latvia stood at EUR 80/MWh, while in Estonia it was EUR 59/MWh. Deividas Šikšnys, head of market development at Litgrid, says electricity prices in the Baltic countries in August were influenced by changing wind conditions in Northern Europe and slightly lower renewable energy generation. In August, electricity demand in Lithuania reached 1,067 gigawatt hours (GWh), which is 1% less than in July. In total, 929 GWh of electricity was generated in Lithuania in August, by 4% less than the previous month, when electricity generation amounted to 969 GWh. Local power plants ensured 87% of the country’s electricity demand. According to preliminary Lithuanian production data, wind power plants generated the most electricity in August – 41% of Lithuania’s total production – but their generation decreased by 2%, to 384 GWh. Solar power generation also decreased by 4%, to 365 GWh. Thermal power plants generated 65 GWh, hydropower plants 72 GWh, and other power plants 42 GWh of electricity. Total electricity imports in August increased by 2%, reaching 389 GWh. According to Litgrid, in August, 59% of electricity imports came from Sweden, 36% from Latvia, and 5% from Poland. Meanwhile, electricity exports decreased by 17%, to 244 GWh. The largest share of exports, 45%, went to Poland, 37% to Sweden, and the remaining 18% to Latvia.
